Run a FLOP validator

devnet · next · development

Last updated 2026-11-03

Run a FLOP validator

Existing validators should use the upgrade manual for rolling image updates, quorum, data preservation and rollback. Do not repeat new-validator registration or change genesis during an upgrade.

FLOP validators author blocks with BABE, vote on finality with AlephBFT, and serve assigned data through a DA worker. No GPU or TEE is needed.

Join the current devnet

Availability checked 3 November 2026: the advertised 0.2.0-devnet.1 package and checksum return 404. Stop before host setup until the validator page offers a verified versioned download. The prepared 0.3.0-devnet.1 source is unpublished and is not an alternative public download. No verified operations intake channel or response deadline is published. Follow public issue #10 (duplicate download report #15) for availability; an issue or interest-form submission does not grant admission. Share only hostname and public SS58 when an official intake route is confirmed, never private keys.

Once a release is published, verify its checksum and follow its README on a dedicated Linux amd64 host. The administrator-assisted sequence is:

  1. Prepare and send two public values. Verify the package checksums, install its dependencies with pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts, then run pnpm onboard prepare. Send only the printed hostname and public SS58 address to FLOP operations. Private account files and keys stay on your host.
  2. Receive access and funding, then join. Operations provides private-network enrollment instructions and funds the account above the live minimum with surplus for fees and DA deposits. After both are confirmed, run pnpm onboard join and tell operations ready. The command waits for sync, registers with owner-bound keys, and restores safe loopback RPC before reporting ready. Registration locks stake. Stop and contact operations after a failed/partial submission; do not blindly rerun signed actions.
  3. Operations checks and activates. Operations reads registration, public session keys, queue position and DA endpoint from finalized chain state and checks the named host's connectivity before promotion. You do not send keys, transaction hashes or configuration. After activation is confirmed, run pnpm onboard verify against your own node. “Ready” does not mean active: session/BABE/Aleph keys and advancing finality must be verified.

The 0.2.0-devnet.1 configuration uses private-network P2P TCP 30333 and host DA TCP 7000, mapped to container TCP 7000; its DA_PORT and DA_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT must agree. The prepared 0.3.0 network inputs use host DA TCP 7001. Use the published package's own port mapping rather than mixing these profiles. RPC 9944 and metrics 9615 remain on loopback. The existing devnet still needs operations approval, funding and promotion. Self-service public testnet onboarding (public P2P and DA, self-service sponsorship, activation without administrator promotion) is still in progress; it is not available merely by selecting testnet in a command.

Select the prepared public-testnet profile

The next prepared validator package retains administrator-assisted-devnet as its default. For example, pnpm onboard prepare --profile administrator-assisted-devnet uses the existing operations-assisted flow. For read-only preflight, run pnpm onboard preflight --profile public-testnet.

This fails closed while public identity, supported image digests, peer endpoints and launch receipts are unset. It starts no service, generates no key and submits no transaction. The prepared package's PUBLIC-TESTNET.md describes versioned network inputs, the standalone public P2P/filtered DA Compose profile and the exact remaining operator handoff. The next package is unpublished; the older administrator-assisted download is currently unavailable.

Signed validator sponsorship requests may auto-admit within the chain-backed sponsored count/stake caps; validators no longer need the former sponsorship allowlist. Devnet miners are admitted automatically too, within a cap on uncalibrated ones; testnet miners still need review. Other launch gates for outside validators remain open, among them committee-eligibility hardening and authenticated finality gossip. The network operator must still authorize public exposure and publish the reviewed network identity. Its clean external host must sync without VPN credentials, see advancing finality, serve assigned DA custody/audit or repair work to existing validators, and show that private RPC, unsafe methods, metrics and internal services are inaccessible. Local fixtures and HTTP health checks cannot establish that acceptance.

Other networks and disposable rehearsals

The remainder is the engineering reference for new disposable networks, not instructions to create a new genesis or use //Alice on the existing live devnet. Public testnet/mainnet operators need their own reviewed network inputs and admission policy.

Input from network operatorPublic placeholderDevnet rehearsal
Chain and genesis<CHAIN_SPEC_URL_OR_FILE> and published genesis hashCommon flop-devnet-N preset or reviewed raw spec
Software<PINNED_NODE_IMAGE> and <PINNED_DA_IMAGE>Two pinned images from one release
Peer discovery<BOOTNODE_MULTIADDRESS>Reachable multiaddress from an existing host
AdmissionPublished funding, stake, queue, and promotion policyDevnet root funds and promotes
Monitoring<PUBLIC_EXPLORER_URL> and <TELEMETRY_URL>Local RPC and metrics

The bracketed values are placeholders, not live addresses. Stop if a required input is missing or if chain spec, genesis, and software release do not agree. Current devnet admission is administrator controlled. It is not an open public onboarding service.

Prepare the host

Use Linux with Docker Engine, the Docker Compose plugin, curl, and jq installed. The join helper also needs Node.js and pnpm matching the repository's pinned toolchain. Give each validator its own persistent volumes and session keys. Protect the host and backups with encrypted storage and key-only SSH. Keep node RPC on loopback, metrics on loopback or a private network, and permit P2P and DA traffic only along the required peer routes. Never run two active processes with the same session keys: simultaneous voting can equivocate. For production planning, the current FLOP profile is 8 dedicated cores, 32 GB RAM, 4 TB NVMe including DA custody, and a reliable low-latency 1 Gbps link. These are planning estimates, not measured devnet minimums. Aleph Zero's hardware reference emphasizes fast I/O and reliable networking, but its storage sizes omit FLOP's DA custody.

From a FLOP repository checkout, make an untracked env file on each host:

cp infra/devnet/.env.example infra/devnet/.env
chmod 600 infra/devnet/.env

Set the fields in that host's infra/devnet/.env:

CHAIN=flop-devnet-6
FLOP_NODE_IMAGE=<PINNED_NODE_IMAGE>
FLOP_DA_VALIDATOR_IMAGE=<PINNED_DA_IMAGE>
HOST_IP=<REACHABLE_HOST_IP>
P2P_PORT=30333
PUBLIC_ADDR=/ip4/<REACHABLE_HOST_IP>/tcp/30333
BOOTNODES=<BOOTNODE_MULTIADDRESS>
DA_PORT=7000
DA_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT=http://<REACHABLE_HOST_IP>:7000
RPC_BIND_IP=127.0.0.1
RPC_METHODS=safe

Use the same chain preset or raw spec and pinned images on all hosts. For a raw spec, such as the one in an operator release bundle, set CHAIN_SPEC_FILE to its host path and CHAIN=/chainspec/chain.raw.json; any other CHAIN boots a built-in preset. Leave BOOTNODES empty for the first genesis host. For a disposable genesis host, set GENESIS_SEED to its distinct //Validator1 through //ValidatorN preset and set DA_VALIDATOR_SEED to the matching secretSeed derived with that same pinned node image. Later joiners leave GENESIS_SEED empty and use a fresh private 32-byte sr25519 seed for DA_VALIDATOR_SEED and their account. Never commit filled env files or send seeds in public tickets. An existing five-authority chain cannot simply switch to the six-authority preset; that requires a new genesis. For a genesis host only, derive its matching DA seed from the pinned image without printing it to the terminal (run from the repository root, after filling .env):

(
  set -euo pipefail
  cd infra/devnet
  set -a; . ./.env; set +a
  test -n "$GENESIS_SEED"
  install -d -m 700 "$HOME/.local/share/flop"
  umask 077
  docker run --rm --entrypoint zkv-relay "$FLOP_NODE_IMAGE" \
    key inspect "$GENESIS_SEED" --output-type json \
    | jq -er .secretSeed > "$HOME/.local/share/flop/genesis-da-seed"
)

Put the saved secret in this host's private DA_VALIDATOR_SEED field using a local editor. Protect or remove the extra seed file after its backup policy is settled. The repository's docs/runbooks/devnet-add-validator.md has more chain-specific rehearsal detail.

Start the first host and get its peer ID from its local RPC:

cd infra/devnet
docker compose config --quiet
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps
curl -fsS -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"system_localPeerId","params":[]}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:9944 | jq -r .result

On every host, compare the local genesis hash with the network operator's independently supplied EXPECTED_GENESIS_HASH (a public value). Do this before funding or registering. A new devnet's administrator must first review the raw chain spec and publish that expected hash; copying an unreviewed host's result as the expectation does not establish chain identity.


FLOP · Run a FLOP validator › Still in infra/devnet; supply the published public hash first.

# Still in infra/devnet; supply the published public hash first.
(
  set -euo pipefail
  : "${EXPECTED_GENESIS_HASH:?set the independently published genesis hash}"
  actual_genesis_hash=$(curl -fsS -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"chain_getBlockHash","params":[0]}' \
    http://127.0.0.1:9944 | jq -er .result)
  test "$actual_genesis_hash" = "$EXPECTED_GENESIS_HASH" || {
    echo 'Genesis mismatch; stop before funding or joining' >&2
    exit 1
  }
)

Continue only when this check exits successfully on that host.

Set each later host's BOOTNODES to a reachable /ip4/<host>/tcp/<port>/p2p/<peer-id> address, then start its Compose project. Open P2P and DA ports to the relevant hosts. A Docker container name is not a cross-host bootnode. The DA worker connects to its own node inside Compose; the advertised DA endpoint must be reachable by other validators. Bring up all genesis authorities promptly: an incomplete genesis committee may leave the finalized head stationary.

Join after genesis

The applicant keeps the account/DA seed, node session keys and node key on their own host. Before initial devnet funding, give the administrator the hostname and public account address. Operations checks the reviewed network inputs and enrolled host identity before funding. After the applicant's local join generates session keys and registers the account, say ready; operations reads public session-key and admission evidence from finalized chain state. fund, promote, and optional refresh use the administrator's root signer and OPERATOR_ADDRESS; read-only verify uses the address alone. Only the applicant's local join needs OPERATOR_SEED. A public deployment still needs its own published admission policy and release inputs.

For an independently held applicant account on the disposable devnet, follow this order:

  1. Generate a fresh private account seed on the joining host and set it as DA_VALIDATOR_SEED. Leave GENESIS_SEED empty. Start the node and DA worker with the same chain and pinned images as the existing hosts.
  2. Fund the account above the live greater of minimumValidatorStake and valueCoupledStakeFloor, with extra for fees. The devnet helper's fund action uses sudo(balances.forceSetBalance); the faucet cannot cover this floor.
  3. Temporarily recreate the joining validator with RPC_METHODS=unsafe while its host RPC remains bound to 127.0.0.1. Run the helper's join action locally. It calls author_rotateKeysWithOwner, checks the keystore, submits session.setKeys with the ownership proof, and calls validators.register. Restore RPC_METHODS=safe immediately; do not put unsafe in .env.
  4. Registration freezes exactly the effective minimum; surplus remains spendable for fees and DA endpoint deposits. Fund again only if that surplus is insufficient. Root reviews the generated public session-key and admission evidence, queue order and the current floor before its promote action submits sudo(validators.rotate(0, 1)). Registration alone only queues the account; candidates below the current floor remain queued.
  5. Run the helper's verify action after promotion. It waits for session activation, checks live BABE and Aleph keys, peers, and advancing finalized height.

The exact executable helper commands are in docs/runbooks/devnet-add-validator.md in the devnet operator checkout. That path is part of the devnet operator checkout; access to private images and network inputs still requires the network operator. The helper runs from sdk/miner-worker after pnpm install --frozen-lockfile at repo root. Never put a private account or root seed into an issue, chat, command log, or shared shell history.

Install the helper's dependencies once on each host that runs it. On the administrator host, set APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS to the reviewed SS58 address and fund it with the authorized disposable devnet root:

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
cd sdk/miner-worker
: "${APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS:?set the reviewed public SS58 address}"
OPERATOR_ADDRESS="$APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS" SUDO_SEED=//Alice DEVNET_ACTION=fund \
  node --input-type=module < ../../infra/devnet/operator.mjs

On the applicant host, set OPERATOR_SEED privately from the local account/DA seed. Run join with local key-generation RPC enabled only for this step. The exit trap restores safe methods and checks the running process even if join fails:

pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
cd sdk/miner-worker
(
  set -e
  set +x
  . ../../infra/devnet/.env
  export OPERATOR_SEED="${DA_VALIDATOR_SEED:?set the applicant seed in the private local .env}"
  restore_safe_rpc() {
    (cd ../../infra/devnet && RPC_METHODS=safe docker compose up -d --no-deps --force-recreate validator) || return 1
    (cd ../../infra/devnet && docker compose exec -T validator sh -c "tr '\000' ' ' </proc/1/cmdline") \
      | grep -q -- '--rpc-methods safe'
  }
  trap 'join_status=$?; trap - EXIT; restore_safe_rpc || { echo "Safe RPC restoration failed; isolate port 9944 and repair the validator before continuing" >&2; exit 1; }; exit "$join_status"' EXIT
  (cd ../../infra/devnet && RPC_METHODS=unsafe docker compose up -d --no-deps validator)
  DEVNET_ACTION=join node --input-type=module < ../../infra/devnet/operator.mjs
)

Back on the administrator host, review the queue and promote the applicant. Fund again only if the applicant's spendable surplus cannot cover fees and DA deposits:


FLOP · Run a FLOP validator › Optional: replenish only if the spendable surplus is insufficient.

# Optional: replenish only if the spendable surplus is insufficient.

FLOP · Run a FLOP validator › OPERATOR_ADDRESS="$APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS" SUDO_SEED=//Alice DEVNET_ACTION=fund \

# OPERATOR_ADDRESS="$APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS" SUDO_SEED=//Alice DEVNET_ACTION=fund \

FLOP · Run a FLOP validator › node --input-type=module < ../../infra/devnet/operator.mjs

#   node --input-type=module < ../../infra/devnet/operator.mjs
OPERATOR_ADDRESS="$APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS" SUDO_SEED=//Alice DEVNET_ACTION=promote \
  node --input-type=module < ../../infra/devnet/operator.mjs

Then run verify on the applicant host, against its own node. The peer and finalized-head checks read only the node at WS_URL, so a run from the administrator host would report that host's node and could pass while the applicant's node is down:

: "${APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS:?set this host's public SS58 address, as given to the administrator}"
OPERATOR_ADDRESS="$APPLICANT_PUBLIC_ADDRESS" WS_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:9944 DEVNET_ACTION=verify \
  node --input-type=module < ../../infra/devnet/operator.mjs

Only the trusted devnet root can run fund, promote, or refresh. The helper checks the root key and that the joining account is the next queued candidate. The applicant's seed stays on their host. A public, reproducible validator release bundle is still in preparation.

FLOP session keys are babe (sr25519 block authoring), audi (sr25519 authority discovery), and alp0 (ed25519 AlephBFT). Aleph Zero's operator guides use an Aura key and a separate validator port; those are not FLOP settings. The FLOP Aleph transport uses the node's libp2p peer port.

Verify and operate

The helper's verify action waits up to two BABE session boundaries after promotion. It confirms session.validators, the registered BABE authority key, and the matching Aleph runtime authority key. aleph.currentCommittee alone is an account snapshot, not proof that a finality key is live. Read local health and finality twice:

curl -fsS -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"system_health","params":[]}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:9944 | jq .result
curl -fsS -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"chain_getFinalizedHead","params":[]}' \
  http://127.0.0.1:9944 | jq -r .result
(cd ../../infra/devnet && docker compose logs --tail=100 validator da-validator)

The log command above assumes the shell is still in sdk/miner-worker after the join block. If starting a fresh shell at the repository root, use (cd infra/devnet && docker compose logs --tail=100 validator da-validator).

Healthy peers, no ongoing sync, and a finalized-head change over a short interval show the node is connected and the network is finalizing. The helper checks account membership and key activation. Monitor free disk space, DA availability, peer count, best and finalized heights, and logs; keep metrics private.

Back up the account seed, node keystore and persistent volume, libp2p node key, and DA worker data with controlled access. Test restoration offline. A chain database snapshot alone does not restore signing or DA custody. Pin images during upgrades, move one validator at a time, and re-check peers and finality after each restart. A standby must stay keyless until the original has stopped and cannot sign. Follow the network's published exit and unbonding policy before retiring an active validator.

SymptomCheck
No peersReachable PUBLIC_ADDR, BOOTNODES, P2P firewall, matching chain and genesis
Registered but idlePromotion, two session boundaries, babe/audi/alp0 keys on the local node
Best height rises, finality does notCommittee key activation and peers on independent nodes; shared provider outage
DA worker failsPrivate seed, connection to its local node, advertised DA endpoint, persistent volume
Join RPC failsLocal unsafe-method window for key generation only, then safe mode restored

For the role's stake and committee rules, see Staking and slashing.
